correction.text: Cuba without the Isle of Pines, sovereign from 20 May 1902

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1902-1904: 'Cuba gained formal independence on 20 May 1902, as the Republic of Cuba' (infobox 'Constitution adopted: 20 May 1902'), but Cliopatria has no Republic of Cuba shape before 1905 and draws the whole island (499 cells) as United States land in 1900-1904. The US dossier removes it as occupation. The 1905 shape stands, without the Isle of Pines. The Platt Amendment (12 June 1901) 'guaranteed the United States right to intervene' and the governments 'have been regarded as client state of the United States'.

120,880 km2 against the infobox 110,860 km2 (undated; ratio 1.09): the grid shape includes coastal cells (12 of its 502 cells lie outside the Natural Earth country). The Isle of Pines (Isla de la Juventud, 8 cells) is absent: Cliopatria draws it as United States land from 1898 to 1925, though 'the United States had never exercised sovereignty over the Isle of Pines' (Pearcy v. Stranahan, 1907, Hay-Quesada page). Without the Guantánamo Bay lease, which the page gives without a year.

correction.text: Cuba without the Isle of Pines, under the US Provisional Government from September 1906 to January 1909

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1908-1910: Cliopatria has no Republic of Cuba shape in 1908-1910 and draws the whole island (498 cells) as United States land. The pages say the Provisional Government was 'a Cuban government, conforming, as far as may be, to the constitution of Cuba' under a US provisional governor, with 'about thirty posts' and a Cuban flag flying; the Republic stayed sovereign and Gómez 'took office on 28 January 1909'. The 1905 shape stands; the occupation is a hatched ledger event.

Same outline as 1905 (no cells gained or lost) until the Isle of Pines joins on 23 March 1925. 120,880 km2 against the infobox 110,860 km2 (ratio 1.09). The 1912 rising of the Partido Independiente de Color 'attempted to establish a separate black republic in Oriente Province' without a territory on the page.

123,918 km2: the Isle of Pines adds 8 cells (2,023 km2); the island is 2,204 km2 on the Cuba page. Cliopatria dates it 1926 but the Hay-Quesada Treaty was 'ratified by the United States Senate on March 13, 1925' and 'Effective: 23 March 1925' (ledger). 123,918 km2 against the infobox 110,860 km2 (ratio 1.12). Cliopatria's 8 United States cells here are the Isle of Pines, not Guantánamo, as the US dossier reads them.

120,828 km2: Cliopatria cuts 12 cells (3,035 km2) in Granma and Santiago de Cuba, the Sierra Maestra, for the Cuban Communists row (3,144 km2). The page has the Granma landing at Playa Las Coloradas, Niquero, on 2 December 1956 and the Sierra Maestra fights of 1957 and 1958 but calls no part a rebel state; the carve ends when Batista fled on 1 January 1959 (ledger).

124,490 km2, the 1926 outline plus the Sierra Maestra (12 cells) and 2 cells on the north coast of Ciego de Ávila: the whole island with the Isle of Pines. 124,490 km2 against the infobox 110,860 km2 (ratio 1.12). The official name is still 'the Republic of Cuba'; one state with the Republic of 1902-1958 (Wikidata Q241 for both Names).
Unchanged from 1960. The page lists no territorial change and names no lease year for Guantánamo.

region.text: Cuba without the Isle of Pines

ledger.note: 20 May 1902: the Republic of Cuba is born. 'Cuba gained formal independence on 20 May 1902, as the Republic of Cuba'; first president Tomás Estrada Palma; the Platt Amendment of 12 June 1901 and the Treaty of Relations of 17 February 1903 gave the United States the right to intervene (a client state).

region.text: '45 square miles (117 km2) of land and water on the shore of Guantánamo Bay'

ledger.note: February 1903: Guantánamo Bay is leased to the United States. The Guantanamo Bay Naval Base page lists the agreement 'signed 16 February 1903; 23 February 1903' (second part 2 July 1903) and the base on '45 square miles (117 km2) of land and water'; the Cuba page has 'Under the Platt Amendment, the U.S. leased the Guantánamo Bay Naval Base from Cuba.' The US dossier dates possession to 10 December 1903. [Month, region, source and confidence set by reviewer am-08-h, 2026-10-19; the earlier 30 km radius drew about 2,800 km2.]

region.text: Cuba, with about thirty army posts, headquarters at Camp Columbia west of Havana, most troops in Santa Clara Province

ledger.note: 29 September 1906: the second US occupation. President Palma resigned on 28 September 1906 and the next day Secretary of War William H. Taft established a provisional government and named himself provisional governor; Magoon took over on 13 October; the first army soldiers landed on 6 October. The Liberals had 'orchestrated a revolt in August 1906'.
28 January 1909: José Miguel Gómez takes office and the occupation ends; 'the last American forces leaving the island country on 6 February 1909'.

23 March 1925: the Isle of Pines is recognised as Cuban. The Hay-Quesada Treaty, signed 2 March 1904 'addressing the status of the Isle of Pines', was 'ratified by the United States Senate on March 13, 1925' and took effect on 23 March 1925: 'the U.S. recognized Cuban sovereignty over the territory of the Isle of Pines'.

region.text: the Sierra Maestra zone of Granma and Santiago de Cuba

ledger.note: 1958: the rebels hold the Sierra Maestra. Cliopatria cuts a 3,035 km2 zone in Granma and Santiago de Cuba out of Cuba for 1958; the page has the Granma landing at Niquero on 2 December 1956 and Sierra Maestra fighting: combat on 17 January 1957, a battle that 'spanned from 11 to 21 July 1958', and 29 July 1958 when 'Batista's troops almost destroyed Castro's small army'. The year is Cliopatria's, the zone the page's.

1 January 1959: the rebels take the state. 'He fled Cuba by air for the Dominican Republic just hours later on 1 January 1959'; Urrutia Lleó took office on 3 January and Castro 'arrived in Havana on 8 January'. The Sierra Maestra zone is no longer held against the government.

1959: Batista's Republic becomes the revolutionary government. Urrutia took office as president on 3 January and 'On 16 February ... Castro had assumed the role of prime minister'; the Cuba page still has the state 'officially the Republic of Cuba' and a 1976 constitution; same state and colour (rule 2). Cliopatria's label turns 'Communist Cuba' in 1960.

wars.name: Partido Independiente de Color rebellion
wars.outcome: The party 'attempted to establish a separate black republic in Oriente Province' (1912 on the page's timeline); the page gives no territory held and no outcome.
wars.note: No zone recorded: the page is silent on land held. The Sugar Intervention (1917-1922; 'in 1917, U.S. Marines returned to Cuba to quell a revolution') is on the page as a label only and is not coded as an occupation of any land.

wars.name: Cuban Revolution
wars.outcome: The 26th of July Movement's war from the Moncada attack (infobox 26 July 1953) to 1 January 1959: Batista fled, Castro's forces entered Havana on 8 January 1959 and the Republic's institutions were dismantled.
wars.note: The page lacks a 'free territory' description of the Sierra Maestra and the Second Front; the zone is Cliopatria's.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the frontier. The Isle of Pines is unsettled until the treaty took effect on 23 March 1925; the Guantánamo Bay lease area is not given on the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria has two rows for one state: Republic of Cuba (1905-1959) and Communist Cuba (1960-2024), both Wikidata Q241. The Cuba page has the state 'officially the Republic of Cuba' with no name change and the same shape (the 1960 shape is the 1957 shape plus the Sierra Maestra and 2 coast cells), so this is ONE dossier with both Names and 8 shapes reviewed; the slug communist-cuba (listed to another part of am-08) should not get a dossier. Cliopatria's Cuba 1905-1925 omits the Isle of Pines (8 cells), drawn as US land until Hay-Quesada took effect on 23 March 1925: the US dossier (am-07) reads those 8 cells in 1905-1907 and 1911-1925 as Guantánamo and the Canal Zone, which they are not (they lie at -82.99..-82.62, 21.5..21.9) and its ledger lacks the Isle of Pines loss of March 1925. The US dossier's 1898-1899 cells (8, near Santiago and Guantánamo) are real US landings. Platt Amendment / client state: the Republic page says the governments 'have been regarded as client state of the United States' and the Platt Amendment (12 June 1901, Treaty of Relations 17 February 1903) 'guaranteed the United States right to intervene', replaced by the Treaty of Relations of 29 May 1934 (the page does not say 'abrogated'). No vassal events are coded because a vassal relation is recorded in the suzerain's dossier; the US dossier (am-07) should consider vassal_start 1902 / vassal_end 1934 for Cuba. Page budget 5 of 5 (Republic of Cuba 1902-1959, Hay-Quesada, Second Occupation, Cuban Revolution, Cuba). Not opened: Platt Amendment, Guantánamo Bay Naval Base (the lease year and area), Sugar Intervention troops, Isla de la Juventud's 1978 renaming, the Bay of Pigs. The Cliopatria 1958 carve is the Cuban Communists row. Rulers omitted: the page gives only the first and last presidents. Counterparts: united-states-of-america (am-07), cuban-communists (am-08, written by another part), cuban-nationalists (this part).
